```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))          # analysis/logistic_susie_simulations -> two up
os.chdir("..")                                       # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_susie_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import resultslib as R

pip, cs = R.load_both()
elbo = R.elbo_frame()

METHODS = ["gibss", "cavi"]                           # the two of interest
SER = {"Lstar": 1, "fit_L": 1}                        # single causal, correctly-specified SER

# Restrict pip/cs to the single-effect datasets fit by BOTH methods. CAVI-cf runs 10
# reps/cell, gIBSS 50, on the SAME content-addressed cells; pooling each method over its
# own reps makes CAVI's binned curves 5x noisier and reads as a method difference where
# there is none. Intersecting sample_ids puts every panel on identical data.
# NB: intersect over ALL single-effect fits (fit_L==1), NOT filt=SER (Lstar==1) -- the
# null cells are Lstar==0 (is_null), so a SER-filtered intersection would drop them and
# leave logbf_roc with no negatives. (elbo_scenario_tables already pairs on the sim.)
def _shared_ids(df, methods, filt):
    d = R.apply_filter(df, filt)
    sets = [set(d.filter(pl.col("method") == m)["sample_id"].to_list()) for m in methods]
    return list(set.intersection(*sets))

_ids = _shared_ids(pip, METHODS, {"fit_L": 1, "Lstar": [0, 1]})   # enriched SER (Lstar=1) + nulls (Lstar=0)
pip = pip.filter(pl.col("sample_id").is_in(_ids))
cs = cs.filter(pl.col("sample_id").is_in(_ids))
```

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
n = pip.filter((pl.col("method") == "cavi") & (pl.col("Lstar") == 1) & (pl.col("fit_L") == 1)).height
print(f"gIBSS vs CAVI-cf, single-effect SER, **{n} shared datasets** (36 cells x 10 reps). "
      "Every figure below is on identical data.")
```

## 1. PIP calibration {#sec-pip-cal}

```{python}
#| label: fig-pip-cal
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "PIP calibration, shared datasets. gIBSS and CAVI-cf coincide."
R.pip_calibration(pip, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS)
plt.show()
```

## 2. FDP vs power {#sec-fdp-power}

```{python}
#| label: fig-fdp-power
#| fig-cap: "FDP vs power as the PIP threshold is swept, shared datasets."
R.power_fdp(pip, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS, panel=(3.2, 3.0))
plt.show()
```

## 3. PIP average precision {#sec-ap-ser}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ap-ser
#| output: asis
print(R.ap_setting_tables(pip, setting=["design", "b0", "T"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS))
```

## 4. Enrichment detection by logBFSER {#sec-logbf-roc}

```{python}
#| label: fig-detect-roc
#| fig-cap: "Enrichment-detection ROC (enriched vs matched null, ordered by logBFSER), shared datasets."
R.logbf_roc(cs, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS, label_kind="detect", panel=(3.4, 3.4))
plt.show()
```

## 5. Credible sets - declared (logBF>2) {#sec-cs-ser}

```{python}
#| label: fig-cs-operating-ser
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "Declared (logBF>2) SER 95%-CS coverage / power / median resolved size, shared datasets."
R.cs_operating_dotplot(cs, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cs-scenario-ser
#| output: asis
print(R.cs_scenario_tables(cs, scenario=["design", "b0", "T"], filt=SER,
                           methods=METHODS, min_log_bf=2.0, group="metric"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cs-calibration-ser
#| fig-cap: "SER credible-set reliability (ungated): nominal beta vs empirical coverage, shared datasets."
R.cs_calibration_curve(cs, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS, min_log_bf=float("-inf"),
                       title="SER credible-set calibration (ungated)")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cs-calibration-ser-declared
#| fig-cap: "SER credible-set reliability at logBFSER>=2, shared datasets."
R.cs_calibration_curve(cs, facet=["design"], filt=SER, methods=METHODS, min_log_bf=2.0,
                       title="SER credible-set calibration (logBF>2)")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cs-size-hist-ser
#| column: screen-inset
#| fig-cap: "Declared (logBF>2) SER 95%-CS size distribution, one panel per method, shared datasets."
R.cs_size_histogram(cs, filt=SER, methods=METHODS, min_log_bf=2.0)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fp-size-ser
#| output: asis
print(R.fp_size_table(cs, filt=SER, methods=METHODS, min_log_bf=2.0))
```

#| label: tbl-elbo-ser
